2. Admittedly, the suit land along with other lands belonged to Ghosal Sing and Chandra Nath Singh each having 8 annas share. Ghosal Sing died leaving two sons Darika Nath and Girish Chandra. They each inherited 4 annas share. Chandra Nath died leaving only son Sukmon Singh who inherited the entire 8 annas share of his father. The CS khatian was correctly recorded accordingly in the name of Darika Nath, Girish Chandra and Sukmon. Darika Nath died leaving his son Tara Mohan Barman (the plaintiff) as his only son. Girish Chandra died leaving his heirs in defendants 1-7. The said Sukmon Singh died leaving only son Ananda Mohan (defendant 8). The plaintiff's case, as unfolds from the plaint, is that when rent fallen due Darika Nath brought Rent Suit 27/9 of 1937 under the Bengal Agricultural Debtore Act, 1935 before Rathor Debt Settlement Board within Police Station, Rani Shankail, which was disposed of on 26-9-1938 (para 2 of the plaint). In that case said Sukmon Singh and Girish Chandra relinquished their claim of right and . possession upon the suit holding including suit land in favour of Darika Nath, father of the' plaintiff, refusing to pay arrear rent as debt. Consequently, the Debt Settlement Board gave an award in favour of Darika Nath on payment of the debt by him alone which was subsequently registered with the local Sub-Registrar Office on 22-11-1938. Thus Darika Nath alone became the sixteen annas owner of the suit holding including suit land and began to possess the suit land exclusively. After death of Darika Nath his only son, the plaintiff acquired the same and is in possession by paying rent to the Government. In the SA khatian names of Girish Chandra and Sukomon Singh were wrongly recorded with the name of plaintiff. Plaintiff then filed Misc. Case 69/70 for correction of record and since the case was verbally compromised, the same was withdrawn and dismissed for non-prosecution. Further case of the plaintiff is that although defendant 8 had no interest in the suit land, he sold some lands to defendant 9 out of the suit holding by kabala which is void and illegal. The plaintiff has already exchanged 'Ka' schedule land and also sold 'Gha' schedule land out of total land of SA khatian 251. Remaining 7.39 acres land is suit land which the plaintiff possesses. Since the defendant 9 threatened the plaintiff to dispossess the plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of title. 

 3. Defendants 1-3 filed a written statement earlier admitting the case of the plaintiff. Defendants 4-7 also filed one written statement earlier admitting claim of the plaintiff. Defendants 8-9 have filed a joint written statement contending, inter alia, that Sukmon Singh got 4.53 acres land in his 8 annas share and after his death Ananda (defendant 8) inherited the same. By kabala dated 23-2-1977 he sold 2.20 acres land to defendant 9. SA khatian was correctly prepared in the names of Girish and Sukmon along with the plaintiff. The story of relinquishment of their claim by Girish Chandra and Sukmon is denied and said to be false. Defendants 1-3 and 4-7 subsequently by filing another set of written statements denied the truth of their previously filed written statement and stated that on plea of compromise the plaintiff took their signatures on some blank papers which he converted into written statements in support of his own case fraudulently beyond their knowledge. 

 This sort of relinquishment or nadabi does not create any title in favour of the person to whom it is made as it is not a transfer in the case of immovable property. Even a transfer deed of Nadabipatra does not create any title in favour of the transferee (11 DLR 539 Md. Arabulla vs. Durga Prasad Tribedi; 8 DLR (WP) 133 Shah Banu Begum vs. lftekhur Mohammad Khan). In fact, the alleged relinquishment was not acted upon which is clear from the SA khatian as it has been prepared in the name of all co-sharers Girish and Sukmon, along with the plaintiff and it did not disentitle the heirs of Sukmon and Girish Chandra to claim their share in the suit land. No document or authentic paper is produced by plaintiff to show the relinquishment of their share by Girish Chandra and Sukmon in favour of Darika Nath. It is settled principle of law that relinquishment does not create any title in favour of the person in whose favour relinquishment is made. Note in the document produced as award of the Debt Settlement Board is not sufficient to prove relinquishment. It is also admitted that SA khatian was prepared in the names of Girish Chandra and Sukmon along with the plaintiff which means continuation of the CS record and possession of other co-sharers. So the alleged relinquishment was not acted upon. Plaintiff for correction of record brought Misc. Case 69/70 which was dismissed for non-prosecution on the basis of compromise. But no paper is produced showing if really any compromise was arrived at.
